info.description:
Household task management API.

Conventions callers need:
- Every response is the envelope `{ success, message, data }`.
- `user`, `group` and `task` are addressed by opaque `uid`; every other resource by numeric `id`.
- Timestamps are UTC with no zone suffix — parse as UTC, convert for display.
- Actors are derived from the token; never send a user or member id to identify the caller.
- Errors: 400 validation, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 409 duplicate or violated business rule, 429 rate limited (see `Retry-After`).
- Role requirements are stated per operation and are not modelled in this spec.

post.description:
Adds a user to a group directly. This is platform tooling: a household admin invites people
 by sharing the group's invite code, which is the only route that asks for the joiner's consent.
 Somebody who previously left or was removed is readmitted on their original membership, with
 the role given here; only a current member is refused. A closed account cannot be added.

memberUid.description:
Who the chore is for, by membership UID. Absent or null releases it back to the household
 pool, which is the only way to put a chore down without giving it to somebody else.

AuditEntityResponse.description: What an audit entry is about: the entity's type, and the identifier the API addresses it by.

AuditFieldChange.description: One field an update touched. from and to are present only for a field whose value is safe to keep - most carry the name alone. The same shape is stored in changed_fields and returned to the client, so one Jackson annotation keeps both compact.

field.description: the field's name as the request DTO spells it

from.description: its value before the update, or null when withheld or previously empty

to.description: its value after the update, or null when withheld or now empty

AuditLogPage.description: One page of an audit feed. Its own shape rather than Spring's Page: that one is built for offset paging and serializes a dozen fields a cursor-paged client cannot use.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor to get the next page. null means this page is the last.

total.description: How many entries the caller can reach in this feed in total, pages included.

CategoryCreateRequest.description:
A new category. Everything editable comes from {@link CategoryUpdateRequest CategoryUpdateRequest}; this adds the
 household it belongs to, which is the one thing a later edit cannot change.

color.description: A `#RRGGBB` hex code. The column holds seven characters, so nothing else fits.

CategoryUpdateRequest.description:
The editable state of a category. Carries no household: a category cannot move between them,
 and one that could would take every task classified by it along.

color.description: A `#RRGGBB` hex code. The column holds seven characters, so nothing else fits.

ChangePasswordRequest.description:
Request body for "change password": the current password, the chosen new password, and a
 current second-factor code when the account has two-factor on.

minutes.description:
How long it actually took. Left out, the task's estimate is snapshotted instead, so the
 share is never silently zero for a chore nobody timed.

photoUid.description:
Proof the round was done, signed for this task. Required when the chore asks for proof,
 and refused as a 409 otherwise - a flag nothing enforces is not a rule.

ConnectedAccountsResponse.description:
The caller's sign-in methods: whether a password is set and whether a Google account is linked.
 At least one is always true for an active account (otherwise it couldn't sign in).

googleLinked.description: true if a Google account is linked

passwordSet.description: true if the account has a password

DeactivateAccountRequest.description:
Request body for "deactivate account". The password is required for an account that has one
 (re-authentication) and ignored for a Google-only account, which the valid session confirms.
 A current second-factor code is required when the account has two-factor on.

ErrorResponse.description: The standard envelope, as returned for a failed request.

ForgotPasswordRequest.description: Request body for "forgot password": the email to send a reset link to.

GoogleAuthRequest.description: Request body for "Sign in with Google": the Google ID token plus the OIDC nonce secret.

GroupMemberResponse.description:
A membership as returned by the API. It carries the member's user summary rather than ids, so a
 client can render a household roster from this one response.

photoUid.description: The uid of an upload of yours, already PUT to the bucket; null clears the picture.

GroupResponse.description:
A group as returned by the API. The invite code is a shareable join secret, so it is exposed
 only through {@link com.tasklean.api.domain.group.dto.GroupResponse#forAdmin(Group, long) #forAdmin(Group, long)} — for callers allowed to invite.

myMemberUid.description:
The caller's own membership uid in this household, null when they are not a member - what
 the task board filters by and what an assignee is set to.

former.description:
Whether the membership has ended. A former member appears only when they did work in the
 window, so the rows still sum to the total; they are never listed at zero.

member.description: Who did the work, keyed by their membership - which is what the board's filter takes.

minutes.description: Minutes of work done in the window. Zero for a member who did none.

roundsDone.description: How many rounds they completed in the window.

MemberSummaryResponse.description:
A person as seen inside a household, keyed by their membership — which is what every write in a group scope takes, so what a client reads off a task can be sent straight back.

Deliberately carries no user uid. A member cannot read another account (GET /api/users/{uid} is admin-or-self) and no group-scoped write accepts one, so publishing a globally stable id would only let anyone sharing a household correlate the same person across all of them.

MyGroupResponse.description:
A group as seen by one of its members, carrying that member's own role so a client can decide
 which admin controls to show. The invite code is present only for a group admin.

myMemberUid.description:
The caller's own membership uid in this household - what the task board filters by and what
 an assignee is set to, so a client can answer "mine" without first reading the roster.

NotificationSettingEntry.description:
One entry of a batch update — the same shape the GET returns, so a client can send back the
 list it rendered. Unlike the single-type endpoint, the type travels in the body.

NotificationSettingRequest.description:
Request body for one notification type's channels — a full replace of that entry, so both
 channels are required. The type itself comes from the path, never the body.

NotificationSettingResponse.description: One notification type's delivery channels for the caller.

inApp.description: whether it appears in the in-app notification list

NotificationSettingsBatchRequest.description:
Request body for a batch update: each entry fully replaces that type's channels. Types the
 batch omits are left untouched.

RecoveryCodesResponse.description:
A freshly generated set of recovery codes. Only ever returned once - they are stored hashed, so
 they cannot be shown again.

recoveryCodes.description: the single-use codes, in the order they should be displayed

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Request body for "reset password": the emailed token and the chosen new password.

SetPasswordRequest.description:
Request body for "set password" on a Google-only account: the chosen new password, plus a
 current second-factor code when the account has two-factor on.

SignedUrlResponse.description:
A short-lived URL an uploaded image can be read from. It is a credential, so it is handed to an
 authorized caller per request rather than stored anywhere.

TagCreateRequest.description:
A new tag. Everything editable comes from {@link TagUpdateRequest TagUpdateRequest}; this adds the household it
 belongs to. Any member may create one — a tag is a label somebody found useful, not a setting.

color.description: A `#RRGGBB` hex code. The column holds seven characters, so nothing else fits.

TagUpdateRequest.description:
The editable state of a tag. Carries no household, for the same reason a category does not: a
 tag that could move between them would take every task labelled with it along.

color.description: A `#RRGGBB` hex code. The column holds seven characters, so nothing else fits.

TaskBoardPage.description: One page of a household's task board. Its own shape rather than Spring's Page, whose JSON carries a dozen fields a client never reads and changes between Spring versions.

items.description: The tasks on this page, in the order asked for.

page.description: Which page this is, counting from zero.

size.description: How many tasks a full page holds.

totalPages.description: How many pages the filter yields in total. Zero when nothing matched.

totalTasks.description: How many tasks match the filter across every page.

taskStatus.description:
Where the task stands now that this instance is recorded. Carried on the action's own answer
 so a client need not re-read the task to redraw the card it just acted on.

taskUid.description: The task by its uid, never its row id - an instance is addressed by id, its task is not.

TaskCreateRequest.description:
A new task. Everything editable comes from {@link TaskUpdateRequest TaskUpdateRequest}; this adds the household it
 belongs to, which is the one thing a later edit cannot change. The author is taken from the
 caller's token, never from the request — a task that named its own creator could be attributed
 to anybody.

assignedToUid.description: The membership uid of whoever it is for. Omitted, the task sits in the household's pool.

nextDueDate.description:
When the task is next due. Required for a recurring task, since it is the schedule's only
 anchor — a weekly chore recurs on whichever day this falls on. Carries an offset so the
 stored UTC instant is the one the caller meant.

photoUid.description: An uploaded picture of what "done" looks like, signed for this task's household.

recurrenceType.description: How often the task recurs. Omitted, it happens once.

tagNames.description:
The labels on the task, as a member types them. A name the household does not have yet
 becomes a new tag; one it already has is matched regardless of case, so the same label is
 never added twice. Absent, the task carries no tags — like every other field here, this is
 the task's whole state, not a change to part of it.

TaskHistoryPage.description:
One page of a task's history. Cursor-paged rather than page-numbered, unlike the board: a daily
 chore accumulates a row a day, and nothing about a history needs a page count.

items.description: The instances, most recently recorded first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor to get the next page. null means this page is the last.

total.description: How many instances this task has recorded in total, pages included.

TaskResponse.description:
A task as returned by the API. Carries the people behind its author and assignee rather than
 ids, so a client can render it without a second call. Its tags are passed in rather than read
 off the task: they live in their own join table, which a task entity deliberately knows
 nothing about.

overdue.description: Derived, never stored: a stored flag is wrong from the due moment until something writes.

from.description: The window actually used, in UTC - the caller's range, or the current week by default.

members.description: Every active member, plus any former one with work in the window. Busiest first.

totalMinutes.description: The sum of the rows, so a share of the total needs no second call.

TaskUpdateRequest.description:
The editable state of a task. Carries neither its group nor its author, because an edit can
 change neither, and no status — completing and archiving are their own operations.

assignedToUid.description: The membership uid of whoever it is for. Omitted, the task sits in the household's pool.

nextDueDate.description:
When the task is next due. Required for a recurring task, since it is the schedule's only
 anchor — a weekly chore recurs on whichever day this falls on. Carries an offset so the
 stored UTC instant is the one the caller meant.

photoUid.description: An uploaded picture of what "done" looks like, signed for this task's household.

recurrenceType.description: How often the task recurs. Omitted, it happens once.

tagNames.description:
The labels on the task, as a member types them. A name the household does not have yet
 becomes a new tag; one it already has is matched regardless of case, so the same label is
 never added twice. Absent, the task carries no tags — like every other field here, this is
 the task's whole state, not a change to part of it.

TwoFactorConfirmRequest.description:
Request body for an operation that weakens or replaces an active second factor (turning it off,
 regenerating recovery codes): both the account password and a current second-factor code, so
 neither a stolen session nor a stolen password is enough on its own. The password is required
 for an account that has one and ignored for a Google-only account.

TwoFactorEnableRequest.description:
Request body for confirming setup: the code currently shown by the authenticator app that was
 just enrolled. No password - the pending secret itself is the proof.

TwoFactorEnableResponse.description:
The result of turning two-factor on: the one-time recovery codes, plus a fresh session for the
 current device because enabling signs every other device out.

recoveryCodes.description: the single-use codes, shown to the user only here

refreshToken.description: the new refresh token for the current device

token.description: the new access token for the current device

TwoFactorSetupRequest.description:
Request body for starting two-factor setup. The password re-authenticates the caller; it is
 required for an account that has one and ignored for a Google-only account, which the valid
 session confirms.

TwoFactorSetupResponse.description:
What the client needs to enroll an authenticator app. The factor is not active yet - it becomes
 active only once a code from it is confirmed.

otpauthUri.description: the otpauth://totp/... URI to render as a QR code

secret.description: the Base32 secret, for manual entry when a QR code can't be scanned

TwoFactorStatusResponse.description: The caller's two-factor state, enough for the settings screen to decide what to show.

confirmedAt.description: when the factor was confirmed; null while it isn't enabled

enabled.description: true if a confirmed second factor is required at sign-in

pendingSetup.description:
true if setup was started but never confirmed, so the client can
                                offer to resume it

recoveryCodesRemaining.description: how many unused recovery codes are left; 0 when not enabled

TwoFactorVerifyRequest.description:
Request body for finishing a sign-in that needs a second factor: the opaque challenge token the
 login response returned, plus a code from the authenticator app or one recovery code.

contentType.description:
The image's type. JPEG, PNG and WebP only, and anything else is refused before a signature
 exists — no SVG, which is a script container rather than a photo.

purpose.description: What the image is for; it decides who may ask for the upload.

sizeBytes.description: The exact byte count the upload will send; it is signed, so it has to be known up front.

targetUid.description: The uid of what the image is for — a group for a group photo, your own user for an avatar.

UploadResponse.description: A signed upload. The caller PUTs the bytes straight to uploadUrl with exactly the content type and length it asked for, then sends uid on the entity it belongs to.

UserRequest.description:
A profile edit: the name parts and the uid of an uploaded photo. A photo URL is not accepted - an
 image of ours is attached by upload uid, never pasted as a link, which is the change V25 already
 made for group photos. The sign-in address is not a profile field either.

photoUid.description:
The uid of a user-photo upload of yours, already PUT to the bucket; null clears ours so the
 Google picture shows again. Only the subject may send it - never an admin editing someone.

UserResponse.description: A user's own profile, or one read by platform staff. Exactly one of photoUid and photoUrl is ever set - see ProfilePhoto.

UserSettingsRequest.description: Request body for replacing the caller's settings — a full PUT, so both fields are required.

locale.description: the UI language (lowercase the name for the BCP-47 tag)

UserSummaryResponse.description:
The slice of a user that other people are allowed to see — enough to render them in a list. Deliberately omits email and account state; those belong to the account's owner and to staff.

Exactly one of photoUid and photoUrl is ever set - see ProfilePhoto.
